note: Per-card-type warm-throughput baselines for the perf-regression gate (scripts/perf_regression.py). The file nests one models block per card type under a 'cards' key (p150a, p300c, ...); the gate detects the card it is running on at runtime (tt-smi / kernel sysfs, mirroring tt_bio/main.py::_detect_p300_devices) and compares only against the matching card's baseline. Under each card-type key an optional 'machines' map keys baselines by physical machine id (socket.gethostname(), the repo's existing convention in tt_bio/runtime.py); the gate resolves a model's baseline from cards.<card_type>.machines.<machine_id>.models first and falls back to cards.<card_type>.models if no machine-specific entry exists for the detected machine. This guards within-card-type machine variance — e.g. qb1's p150a cards read ~30-36% slower than pc's p150a on the same models, so a baseline seeded on pc reads as a false regression on qb1 (and vice versa); a machine-specific entry overrides the card-level fallback per model, so a card type does not need a full per-machine block, only the models that actually differ per machine. A P300c baseline must never be judged against a P150a run — the P150 is a smaller chip and would read as a false 20-34% regression that is just the card, not the code. If a detected card type has no recorded baseline yet the gate FAILS loudly (every model NO BASELINE) rather than silently skipping. Protocol: scripts/perf_regression.py --model <m>; fold models fold examples/trpcage.yaml (20 aa, single-sequence) at 1 recycling cycle / 10 sampling steps / 1 diffusion sample; esmc-600m embeds 8x ubiquitin (76 aa) at batch 8; esmc-6b embeds 8x ubiquitin (76 aa) one-sequence-at-a-time (batch 1 nominal) -- the 6B sharded-TransformerEngine backbone (~13 GB resident) ignores batch_size and runs sequentially, so its seq/s is per-sequence throughput on a different runtime shape than 300m/600m, gated separately; boltzgen runs `tt-bio gen run examples/binder.yaml` (protein-anything, 4 designs) end-to-end and reports designs/s = num_designs / wall-clock (a single pipeline invocation, not a warm loop — the first design's first-kernel compile is included, so this is a conservative cold-inflated warm-throughput proxy; the cold fraction is stable across releases). Each fold/embed model: load once in-process, 2 warmup folds (absorb first-kernel compile, excluded), 5 timed folds, report median throughput. Model load + first-compile are excluded — this is a warm dispatch/throughput number, not a cold-start or production fold. It catches kernel/dispatch regressions; accuracy is scripts/release_gate.py's job. Update a baseline only via --update-baseline --note "<why this perf change is intended>" on a card of that type; never silently. Seed a new card type by running the gate on that card with --update-baseline; --update-baseline writes to the detected machine's machine-specific block so every baseline is tagged with the machine that produced it.

protenix-v1.note: first protenix-v1 perf cell, p300c / tt-quietbox2 card 0, tt-bio 0.7.2 tree (480ae2df). v0.7.2 declined to seed this cell because two draws read 3.20726 and 3.292402 structures/s, 2.65% apart, over that pass pre-registered 2% bar. Characterised here with 11 fresh-process draws (10 of them back-to-back under benchlock on an idle box): median 3.3279, band 3.256117-3.352770, i.e. 2.97% between the extremes, with 9 of 10 benchlocked draws inside a 1.66% band. Two noise components are separable in the raw folds. An occasional slow tail fold inside a process (1-2 of the 5 land up to 3% high, e.g. draw 8 at 0.2978/0.2980/0.2983/0.2986/0.3069 s) is absorbed by the median of 5. A whole-process offset is not: draw 7's FASTEST fold (0.3047 s) is slower than draw 4's SLOWEST (0.2994 s), two processes 40 s apart on the same idle box with non-overlapping fold distributions. That second component is what makes a two-draw agreement test a coin flip, and it is fixed by more draws, not by more warmup; the 15% gate still has ~5x headroom over the worst observed draw-to-draw excursion, so the cell is meaningful. Cross-check on the same box and session: protenix-v2 3.118 and opendde 2.843 against 3.024 and 2.895 measured on the previous physical qb2 at the same tag, i.e. the replacement hardware reproduces the old box to within 3%, so this cell is comparable to the numbers v0.7.2 recorded.

The 300m/600m batch-8 legs and esmc-300m-single are 785f0456 (the worker embed path moved onto the already-shipped threaded write_npz_many; that commit measured the old 16.737 seq/s baseline as 90.5% host zlib on this exact card, 47.13 ms device against 446.79 ms serial write). esmc-300m-single also carries 3bb206e7 (B=1 ttnn trace capture, 1.47x). esmc-6b is 2907613b (81 blocking device->host copies per forward cut to 1) on top of the same write fix. Measured on qb1 card 2 under the pinned release runtime (ttnn 0.68.0, torch 2.13.0). CAVEAT: these legs still time the whole predict_one wall, so roughly half of each is host zlib, and draw-to-draw spread on a busy qb1 measured 5-35% (esmc-300m 67.26/53.08, esmc-600m 61.83/58.93, esmc-300m-single 34.89/38.52, esmc-6b 6.31/8.54 seq/s over two draws) -- wider than the +-15% threshold. Take a second draw before believing a FAIL here. The structural fix is to gate the device_s that tt_bio/worker.py already reports separately, not the whole wall.

Draw spread 2-15%, and every leg clears its old number by 60-290%, far outside that. esmc-600m had no pc entry at all and was reading the 07-17 card-level 20.92; it has one now. The old pc boltz2-affinity seed of 0.005688 (175.8 s) is confirmed an outlier: an idle pc runs the leg in 46-53 s, close to qb1's 63.65 s. The ESM-C legs time all of predict_one, roughly half of which is host zlib, so they inherit fleet load: on a busy qb1 the same legs spread 34-37%. Take a second draw before believing a FAIL here.

rfd3.note: refresh the stale 07-26 pc entry (0.122207). Nine characterisation draws on an idle pc before this one, each itself a median of 3 end-to-end runs: 0.1632 0.1809 0.1914 0.1932 0.1989 0.2029 0.2049 0.2051 0.2116 designs/s, median 0.1989, band about -18%/+6% around it with the 0.1632 draw the one low tail. The value here is a further draw from that band. It was not taken as the first draw that came: the first --update-baseline attempt landed on 0.1632 and was rejected, because a low seed silently stops guarding (it would have let a real 15% regression through) while a high one false-alarms on the tail. Every draw beats the old number by 33-73%, so the gain itself is not in question. Attributed to the rfd3 kernel work between the 07-26 seed and now (703d12a1 sparse bias one-pass, 923a9396 fused score+bias, fa7246da/881704d2 multiplicity-batched bias, 4ed029d3 step-invariant uploads, 2438b0e5 DiT dense tail, adbd5943 L1-resident pair Transition). Single-shot leg: treat a FAIL as unproven until a same-card A/B against the merge base reproduces it.

esmc-300m.note: pc machine-entry backfill, see tt-bio-perf-baseline-refresh-pc-half2: these four legs had no cards.p150a.machines.pc entry and were reading the stale 07-17/07-19 card-level fallback, which a real regression of up to the model's own landed gain would still pass. Draws on an idle pc before this write: esmc-300m 102.40/100.28 seq/s, esmc-6b 9.181/9.213 seq/s, esmfold2 2.245/2.419/2.249 structures/s, esmfold2-fast 2.864/2.850/2.819 structures/s. Every leg clears its old number by 23-512%, an order of magnitude outside its own draw spread (0.3-7.6%). The ESM-C legs time all of predict_one, part of which is host npz work, so they inherit fleet load: the same legs spread 34-37% on a loaded qb1. Take a second draw before believing a FAIL. The gains are attributed to 785f0456 (embed npz compression was 85-90% of an ESM-C job) and 2907613b (6B forward copied back 81 hidden states) for the ESM-C pair, and to the esmfold2 L1/row-blocking series (8b6493b8, fcd1a088, dffb853b, 5225b579, a22e2ec2) for the fold pair.

esmfold2-fast.note: pc machine-entry backfill, see tt-bio-perf-baseline-refresh-pc-half2: esmfold2-fast had no cards.p150a.machines.pc entry and was reading the stale 07-17 card-level 2.29, so a real regression of up to a quarter of the leg's throughput still passed on pc. Five draws on an idle pc, in order: 2.864 / 2.850 / 2.819 / 2.612 / 2.644 structures/s. The value here is the median (the third draw, 355 ms/call), not the last --update-baseline measurement. Both --update-baseline attempts landed in the low 2.6 half of the band and were rejected: at the +-15% threshold a 2.62 seed only FAILs below 2.23, which is under the old 2.29 baseline, i.e. a complete loss of the landed gain would still PASS. The median seed FAILs below 2.40 and does catch that. The two 2.6 readings came after the two 2.8 ones on the same card within 15 minutes, so treat the band as ~9% wide and drifting, not as one outlier. Gain over 07-17 is 15-25% depending on the draw. Attributed to the esmfold2 L1/row-blocking series (8b6493b8, fcd1a088, dffb853b, 5225b579, a22e2ec2).
